facts.text: The Pacific black duck has a dark body with a paler head, dark crown and facial stripes.
facts.quote: It has a dark body, and a paler head with a dark crown and facial stripes.

facts.text: In flight it shows a green speculum and pale underwing.
facts.quote: In flight, it shows a green speculum and pale underwing.

facts.text: The female quacks in a raucous, rapid sequence that decreases in volume.
facts.quote: the Pacific black duck is one of a number of duck species that can quack, with the female producing a sequence of raucous, rapid quacking which decreases in volume.

facts.text: It is mainly vegetarian, feeding on seeds of aquatic plants, plus small crustaceans, molluscs and aquatic insects.
facts.quote: The Pacific black duck is mainly vegetarian, feeding on seeds of aquatic plants. This diet is supplemented with small crustaceans, molluscs and aquatic insects.

facts.text: It dabbles by plunging its head underwater and upending, raising its rear end vertically out of the water.
facts.quote: Food is obtained by 'dabbling', where the bird plunges its head and neck underwater and upends, raising its rear end vertically out of the water.

facts.text: The nest is usually placed in a hole in a tree, though old corvid nests or the ground are sometimes used.
facts.quote: The nest is usually placed in a hole in a tree, but sometimes an old nest of a corvid is used and occasionally the nest will be placed on the ground.

facts.text: The female alone incubates the clutch of 8–10 pale cream eggs, which hatch after 26–32 days.
facts.quote: The clutch of 8–10 pale cream eggs is incubated only by the female. The eggs hatch after 26–32 days.

facts.text: Downy ducklings can fly when around 58 days of age.
facts.quote: The precocial downy ducklings leave the nest site when dry and are cared for by the female. They can fly when around 58 days of age.

facts.text: It is found in Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand and many islands of the southwestern Pacific.
facts.quote: is a dabbling duck found in much of Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and many islands in the southwestern Pacific

facts.text: It has declined sharply in New Zealand due to competition and hybridisation with the introduced mallard.
facts.quote: The Pacific black duck has declined sharply in numbers in New Zealand and several Australian islands due to competition from and hybridisation with the introduced mallard.
